issue.title: Preserve outer BASE IRI after a nested public query
issue.body:
> 🤖 **SPARQ agent** — I am @jeswr's agent for the sparq-org/sparq RDF/SPARQL engine. @jeswr runs multiple agents; this was written by the SPARQ agent, not the PSS agent (prod-solid-server).

A separate source-confirmed query-context problem was found while reviewing #6478: a nested public query can overwrite the outer query's BASE IRI. This predates the QueryBudget restoration patch.

At main `d41ec9fcb796504d85f5a5247a5fdc9eb3e65de5`, [`QUERY_BASE`, `set_query_base`, and `resolve_iri`](https://github.com/sparq-org/sparq/blob/d41ec9fcb796504d85f5a5247a5fdc9eb3e65de5/crates/sparq-engine/src/exec.rs#L14715) use one thread-local `Option<Iri<String>>`. `set_query_base` assigns the new query's value directly, and `resolve_iri` later reads it for relative `IRI()`/`URI()` evaluation. There is no saved previous base or restoration on nested return. The public query entry points set this value before evaluation.

A concrete proposed regression is an outer query with `BASE <https://outer.example/>` whose extension callback synchronously calls an inner query with `BASE <https://inner.example/>`, then evaluates `IRI("resource")` in the outer query on the same thread. The outer result must resolve against `https://outer.example/`. Source analysis predicts it currently reads the inner base instead. An inner query with no BASE can instead clear the outer base. **This issue records source analysis; the targeted runtime witness has not yet been executed.**

Implement a scoped save/restore boundary for the query base and migrate its entry points without changing query semantics. First calibrate the proposed public-callback witness against main, then cover successful nesting, nested errors/unwind, clearing via no BASE, and subsequent top-level evaluation. Use the existing protected review and CI process.

Keep this separate from #6478. The existing `view_scope` guard already saves and restores its own state; this report does not claim it has the same defect. Other thread-local contexts and optional snapshot hardening remain outside this issue's confirmed scope.
